assumptions: Hourly simulation over one typical year (Munich PVGIS TMY, pvlib), household load BDEW H25 with single-home scatter.
Electricity 37 ct/kWh, rising 2% a year; feed-in 7.7 ct up to 10 kWp, 6.66 ct above.
Battery 90% usable, 90% round trip, greedy self-consumption.
EV 2,700 kWh a year at 18 kWh/100 km, charged from 18:00.
Heat pump EUR 33,500 less the 30% BEG base subsidy on up to EUR 28,000, less EUR 10,000 for the boiler replacement it avoids: EUR 15,100 counted.
Heat pump 5,882 kWh a year: 20,000 kWh heat (heating cost over 12 ct per kWh of heat) at JAZ 3.4.
No feed-in pay in the 573 sunniest hours (negative prices, 2025); upkeep 1.5% of PV and battery cost a year.
NPV over 20 years at 3% discount, 0.5% a year PV degradation; battery replaced after 15 years (15 years or 6,000 cycles).
PV EUR 2,333 plus EUR 883 per kWp (EUR 1,350 per kWp at 5 kWp, 1,000 at 20 kWp); battery EUR 315 per kWh.
Replay of calendar 2025: Munich hourly weather from the Open-Meteo historical API (ECMWF IFS, CC BY 4.0), PV through the same pvlib chain as the typical year.
Day-ahead prices DE-LU from Energy-Charts (Fraunhofer ISE; Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de, CC BY 4.0), 15-minute prices from October averaged per hour.
Retail price stays the fixed tariff in every hour (no dynamic tariff simulated); feed-in is the fixed EEG rate, the spot price only decides when it is paid.

No feed-in pay in negative-price intervals (EEG 2023 section 51 as amended by the Solarspitzengesetz, in force 25 Feb 2025, for new systems); the lost intervals added to the end of the 20-year term (section 51a) are not counted.
Same load, battery, capex and upkeep as the typical year; payback is capex over the 2025 saving.
588 hours with a negative day-ahead interval in 2025; data read from the bundled file.
